'''Amiram Goldblum''' ({{langx|he|עמירם גולדבלום}}; born 22 December 1945) is an Israeli [[chemist]] and activist in the [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]. He is Professor Emeritus of Computational Medicinal Chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] School of Pharmacy. He holds a PhD in [[organic chemistry]] from the Hebrew University. He is the head of the [[Molecular Modelling]] and Drug Design unit at the university's Institute for Drug Research.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://medicine.ekmd.huji.ac.il/en/research/amiramg/Pages/default.aspx|title= Prof. Amiram Goldblum |publisher=The Faculty of Medicine, Hebrew University of Jerusalem |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref>

Goldblum was a leader of [[Peace Now]], served as its spokesperson for 20 years, and constructed the Settlements Watch activities of Peace Now.<ref>{{cite news|title=Settlers willing to leave West Bank, Gaza – survey|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/settlers-willing-to-leave-west-bank-gaza-survey-1.323499|access-date=3 December 2012|newspaper=CBC News|date=25 July 2002}}</ref> Until 2020, he was on the board of the international council of the [[New Israel Fund]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nif.org/about/people |title=People |publisher=New Israel Fund |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref>

==Biography==
Amiram Goldblum was born in [[Rosh Pinna]] in 1945. He is the son of Professor Natan Goldblum, a senior officer in the Medical Corps of the IDF until 1956 and an [[Israel Prize]] recipient (1988) for his lifetime efforts to eradicate viral diseases in Israel, in particular, polimyellitis <ref>{{cite journal |title= Professor Natan Goldblum: The Pioneer Producer of the Inactivated Poliomyelitis Vaccine in Israel |publisher= NIH |date=2010 |pmc = 2951960|last1 = Blum|first1 = N.|last2 = Katz|first2 = E.|last3 = Fee|first3 = E.|journal = American Journal of Public Health|volume = 100|issue = 11|pages = 2074–2075|doi = 10.2105/AJPH.2010.192922|pmid = 20864699}}</ref> a. The family was evacuated to [[Haifa]] during the [[1948 Arab–Israeli War]]. Goldblum's mother Tamar (née Toren) was a member of the [[Irgun]] and had been in the [[Beitar]] youth movement, being instructed by [[Eliyahu Meridor]] (father of Israeli politician and Minister [[Dan Meridor]]). Goldblum attended high school in the [[Hebrew University Secondary School]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2003-06-17 |title=מימשו את הפוטנציאל |url=https://www.haaretz.co.il/misc/2003-06-17/ty-article/0000017f-df1f-df7c-a5ff-df7ff14a0000 |work=הארץ |language=he}}</ref> Goldblum studied [[chemistry]] and [[physics]] at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, as a student of [[Ernst David Bergmann]] and of [[Raphael Mechoulam]], and continued postdoc studies in Paris with [[Bernard Pullman]] and [[Alberte Pullman]] and with [[Corwin Hansch]] in [[Pomona College]] (California).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chembiotec.de/index.php?article_id=779 |title=Amiram Goldblum |publisher=Biotrends |date=2010 |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref> During the years 1970-1979 he served as a news announcer in [[Kol Yisrael]] and as an anchor of classical and jazz music programs on the Israeli Radio. Goldblum joined the [[Hebrew University]] in 1979 and became associate professor of Medicinal Chemistry in 1989 and full professor in 2010 and retired in 2015, becoming Professor Emeritus.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://medicine.ekmd.huji.ac.il/en/research/amiramg/Pages/default.aspx|title= Prof. Amiram Goldblum|publisher=Hebrew University of Jerusalem  |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref> Goldblum is a member of the Supreme Academic Council of the [[Jerusalem Academy of Music and Dance]] and member of the Supreme Academic Council of the AlQasemi Academy in Baka El Gharbieh <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.qsm.ac.il/en/
|title= Academic College of Education|accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref>

Goldblum was married to Israela Weinstein from 1967 until her death in 2006.<ref name=PeaceNow>{{cite news |url=https://www.haaretz.co.il/misc/1.1380369 |script-title=he:סביב שולחן האוכל שלה נולדה "שלום עכשיו" |trans-title=Peace Now started around her table |language=Hebrew |author=Uri Daromi |date=23 January 2007 |newspaper=Haaretz |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref> Goldblum is married to Idit Amihai,  head of Museums and Public Galleries departments of Israel's  Ministry of Culture and Sports.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://bigstory.ap.org/article/israel-museums-hide-art-protect-it-rockets |title=Israel museums hide art to protect it from rockets |author=Dan Balilty |author2=Daniel Estrin |date=19 November 2012 |publisher=Associated Press |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref>

Goldblum's son, Dan Goldblum, who served in the Israeli Commando Unit, [[Sayeret Matkal]], was badly wounded in the commando's preparative operation ([[Operation Bramble Bush]]) to kill Saddam Hussein, on 5 November 1992.<ref>{{cite book|author= עמרי אסנהיים |author-link=Omri Asnheim |script-title=he:צאלים הטראומה של סיירת מטכ"ל |trans-title=Tze'elim, The Trauma of Sayeret Matkal|year=2012 |language=Hebrew |page=8|asin=B00AP1IV0A |publisher=Kinneret}}.</ref> Goldblum's daughter Maya<ref name="PeaceNow"/> served in Sayeret Matkal following her brother.

Goldblum fought in the [[Yom Kippur War]], October 1973, as part of battalion 86  which was attached to armoured Division 460. Goldblum fought with his unit over the Suez Canal, where his unit was fighting inside the Egyptian city of Suez toward the end of the war [[Battle of Suez]].  The story of some of Goldblum's actions during that war was published in 2014.<ref>{{cite journal |title= טופס האפסנאות נשמר בתנאים של בית מרקחת 40 שנה|author=דבורי בורגר |date= June 2014 | publisher = "shirion" no. 45 - בטאון עמותת יד לשריון | page = 84}}</ref>

==Scientific career==
Goldblum invented an [[algorithm]] for solving extremely complex [[combinatorial]] problems, called Iterative Stochastic Elimination (ISE).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rayan |first1=A. |last2=Marcus |first2=D. |last3=Goldblum |first3=A. |url=https://medicine.ekmd.huji.ac.il/En/publications/Publications/Pages/Abstract.aspx?pid=8925&src=https%3a%2f%2fmedicine.ekmd.huji.ac.il%2fEn%2fPublications%2fpublications%2fPages%2fdefault.aspx%3ft%3dIterative+Stochastic+Elimination+%26aut%3dGoldblum%2c+A%26s%3ddesc |title=Predicting oral druglikeness by iterative stochastic elimination |journal=Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling |volume=50 |issue=3 |pages=437–45 |date=22 March 2010 |accessdate=2 March 2014 |doi=10.1021/ci9004354 |pmid=20170135 |archive-date=2 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402164926/https://medicine.ekmd.huji.ac.il/En/publications/Publications/Pages/Abstract.aspx?pid=8925&src=https%3a%2f%2fmedicine.ekmd.huji.ac.il%2fEn%2fPublications%2fpublications%2fPages%2fdefault.aspx%3ft%3dIterative+Stochastic+Elimination+%26aut%3dGoldblum%2c+A%26s%3ddesc |url-status=dead |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://medicine.ekmd.huji.ac.il/en/research/amiramg/Pages/publications.aspx| title= Prof. Amiram Goldblum| publisher=Hebrew University |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref>

Goldblum's ISE algorithm is the basis for two Hebrew University science-related companies that expand on his research and discovery of drug candidates, Pepticom,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pepticom.com/bod.html | title= board of directors|publisher=Pepticom |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref>  and RebioticsRX, focusing on nanomedicine <ref>{{cite web |url=http://rebioticsRX.com | title= Inventors| accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref> He won first prize in the contest of the American Chemical Society Computers in Chemistry Division in the ACS meeting, Washington D.C. 2000 for his new algorithm, which was developed together with PhD student Meir Glick.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://oldwww.acscomp.org/Awards/emerging2000.html |title=Symposium on Emerging Computational Technologies August 2000, Washington D.C. |date=1 July 2011 | publisher=Computers in Chemistry - A Program Division of the American Chemical Society |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref> Goldblum was awarded the Kaye Innovation Prize in 2017 for "dramatic improvements in drug discovery methods".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://new.huji.ac.il/en/article/35036 |title=Algorithm leads to dramatic improvement in drug discovery methods; Prof. Amiram Goldblum wins 2017 Kaye Innovation Award|date=22 June 2017 | publisher=The Hebrew University of Jerusalem |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref> [[Fraunhofer Institute]], the leading European Application oriented research center <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fraunhofer.de/en/jobs-and-career.html| title= Jobs and Career| publisher=Fraunhofer Gesellschaft |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref> opened one of its two first project centers, "Fraunhofer Project center on Drug discovery and delivery" in the labs of Profs. Golomb (drug delivery) and Goldblum (Drug Discovery) at the Institute for Drug Research.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.igb.fraunhofer.de/en/about-us/cooperation/fraunhofer-project-center-for-drug-discovery-and-delivery-at-huji.html| title = Fraunhofer Project Center for Drug Discovery and Delivery @ Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel| publisher=Fraunhofer Gesellschaft |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref>

Goldblum's research is focused on the discovery of new drugs against [[SARS-CoV-2]], on [[Cannabinoids]]<ref>{{cite web|url= https://cannabinoids.huji.ac.il/people/goldblum-phd|title= home/researchers|publisher= The Hebrew University cannabinoids research Multidisciplinary center|accessdate= 29 April 2020|archive-date= 19 September 2020|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200919001430/https://cannabinoids.huji.ac.il/people/goldblum-phd|url-status= dead}}</ref> and the [[Central nervous system|CNS]], and [[obesity]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://new.huji.ac.il/en/article/37855| title= Algorithm leads to dramatic improvement in drug discovery methods; Prof. Amiram Goldblum wins 2017 Kaye Innovation Award| publisher=The Hebrew University |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref>

==Political activism==
Goldblum was the spokesperson of Peace Now from 1980 to 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://archive.peacenow.org/entries/archive229 |title=On Opposite Sides Inside the Same Frame |date=1 February 2005 |publisher=Americans for Peace Now |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref> He was in the front line of the demonstration when Peace Now protester [[Emil Grunzweig]] was murdered. He later identified the incident as a "catalyst" for greater political activism.<ref>{{cite news|last=Galili|first=Lily|title=Avrushmi's parole sparks memories, anger and resignation|url=https://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/news/avrushmi-s-parole-sparks-memories-anger-and-resignation-1.37468|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121207090717/http://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/news/avrushmi-s-parole-sparks-memories-anger-and-resignation-1.37468|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 7, 2012|accessdate=3 December 2012|newspaper=Haaretz|date=8 August 2002}}</ref> Goldblum initiated the Settlements Watch<ref>{{cite web |url=http://peacenow.org.il/eng/content/what-settlement-watch-team |title=What is Settlement Watch Team? |publisher=Peace Now |accessdate=2 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140303190449/http://peacenow.org.il/eng/content/what-settlement-watch-team |archivedate=3 March 2014 }}</ref> activities of Peace Now in 1990.<ref>{{cite book |title=In Pursuit of Peace: A History of the Israeli Peace Movement |author=Mordechai Bar-On |author-link=Mordechai Bar-On |publisher=United States Institute of Peace |date=1996 |isbn=978-1878379535}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |url=http://simania.co.il/bookdetails.php?item_id=11729 |script-title=he:שלום עכשיו |trans-title=Peace Now |language=Hebrew |author=Tzali Reshef}}</ref> In 1995, Goldblum, referring to the Israeli cabinet decision to expand the settlements, said, "We believe that this decision is going to bring a tremendous clash with the Palestinians."<ref>{{cite news |author=Barton Gellman |title=Israeli Cabinet Panel Approves Major Expansion of Settlements |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-817998.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140611073320/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-817998.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=11 June 2014 |newspaper=The Washington Post |access-date=December 3, 2012 |date=26 January 1995|url-access=subscription |via=[[HighBeam Research]]}}</ref> In a 2001 interview after the beginning of the [[Second Intifada]], Goldblum discussed the name of the organization Peace Now, saying "The name is very problematic. Today I would not choose the same name for the movement, but we can't change it now. I find this name extremely difficult and it is even a source of embarrassment for me. I can't even put the movement's sticker on my car."<ref name="jpress">{{cite web |url=http://www.jewishpress.com/news/israel/peach-now-leader-people-think-im-an-idiot/2001/07/20/0/ |author=Giora Eilon |title=Peach [''sic''] Now Leader 'People Think I'm An Idiot' |date=20 July 2001 |publisher=The Jewish Press |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref>

In October 2012, Goldblum and his family foundation, the Yisraela Fund<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nif.org.il/programs/goldbloom |script-title=he:פרס ישראלה גולדבלום |trans-title=Israela Goldblum Prize |language=Hebrew |publisher=New Israel Fund |accessdate=2 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140303132605/http://nif.org.il/programs/goldbloom |archive-date=3 March 2014 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> paid for and were involved (along with other Israeli academics) in commissioning a [[October 2012 Haaretz poll|controversial poll]] regarding Israeli attitudes towards prejudice, along with [[Mordechai Bar-On]], Ilan Baruch, [[Alon Liel]], and  [[Michael Sfard]].<ref name="25 October 2012">{{cite news |last=Jenni |first=Frazer |title=Shock findings of 'apartheid' poll questioned |url=http://www.thejc.com/news/israel-news/88058/shock-%EF%AC%81ndings-apartheid%E2%80%99-poll-questioned |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121027235325/http://www.thejc.com/news/israel-news/88058/shock-%EF%AC%81ndings-apartheid%E2%80%99-poll-questioned |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 27, 2012 |date=25 October 2012 |newspaper=Jewish Chronicle |accessdate=3 December 2012}}</ref> In a press release of the commissioning group, sent by Goldblum, it was stated, "a large part of the Jewish population (58%) accepts the application of the term '[[apartheid]]' to the current state of affairs in Israel. It is, however, not clear what these respondents understand by the term as this question did not require clarification." Goldblum also acknowledged there were problems with a question used on the poll. Israeli statistician Camil Fuchs, who supervised the company that conducted the poll, told ''[[The Times of Israel]]'' that the questions in the poll were fine and did not need changing by the Dialog team.<ref>{{cite news |last=Miller |first=Elhanan |title=Haaretz changes tack on major story that alleged widespread 'apartheid' attitudes in Israel |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/haaretz-changes-tack-on-major-story-that-alleged-widespread-apartheid-attitudes-in-israel/ |accessdate=3 December 2012 |newspaper=The Times of Israel |date=30 October 2012}} Miller adds: "It is, however, not clear what these respondents understand by the term as this question did not require clarification."</ref>

In January 2013 Goldblum was #87 on the candidates list of [[Meretz]], for the [[Knesset]] [[2013 Israeli legislative election|elections]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bechirot.gov.il/elections19/heb/list/List.aspx?ListId=117 |script-title=he:מרצ - השמאל של ישראל |trans-title=Meretz – The Left of Israel |language=Hebrew |publisher=Knesset 19th Election Central Board |accessdate=2 March 2014}} Goldblum no. 87 on the MERETZ list to the 19th Knesset</ref>

In February 2013, Goldblum was one of the organizers of a gathering  at the Van Leer Institute in Jerusalem which discussed apartheid in the Israeli context. A new NGO,  'The Organization for the Prevention of Apartheid in Israel', was established to expose and fight against trends of racism and apartheid in Israel.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://on-the-left-side.org.il/%D7%9E%D7%93%D7%95%D7%A2-%D7%A6%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9A-%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%92%D7%95%D7%9F-%D7%9C%D7%9E%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%A2%D7%AA-%D7%90%D7%A4%D7%A8%D7%98%D7%94%D7%99%D7%99%D7%93-%D7%91%D7%99%D7%A9%D7%A8%D7%90/ |script-title=he:מדוע צריך ארגון למניעת אפרטהייד בישראל |trans-title=Why we need an organization to prevent Apartheid in Israel |language=Hebrew |author=Amiram Goldblum |work=על צד שמאל |date=20 February 2013 |publisher=On the Left Side |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/a-night-of-apartheid/ |title=A night of apartheid |author=Raphael Ahren |date=21 February 2013 |newspaper=The Times of Israel |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2013/04/is-israel-walking-towards-apar-1.html |title=Is Israel Heading Toward Apartheid? |author=Akiva Eldar |date=12 April 2013 |publisher=Israel Pulse |accessdate=2 March 2014}}</ref>

Due to his political views, Goldblum decided in April 2020 to leave the International Council of the [[New Israel Fund]] saying that he "left in order to be free and independent, in order not to attribute to NIF anything that I say which is different than what NIF says". [[New Israel Fund]] denied a report on [[Makor Rishon]] claiming that "NIF dissociated itself from Goldblum in the wake of his derogatory remarks about Israeli settlers and right wing figures". NIF reacted by declaring that "Contrary to what is said in this report, NIF did not take any steps against Prof. Goldblum, Goldblum was not rejected from the International Council, NIF did not dissociate itself from him and did not request to do so. As Goldblum said, he requested to leave on his own will. Prof. Goldblum is a person of countless virtues who devoted all his life to voluntary activism for the sake of Peace and Equality, for the sake of the State of Israel, The Israeli Society and for the New Israel Fund and we thank him for that".<ref>[https://www.makorrishon.co.il/news/221717/ בגלל התבטאויותיו הבוטות: הקרן החדשה מתנתקת מעמירם גולדבלום]</ref>
